football_evidence.question: Can Florida International’s pass rush get to Deshawn Purdie?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Liberty, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.4 of the 5.0 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Liberty has the ball (big plays through the air): Liberty’s offense turns 15.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Florida International’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Liberty has the ball (big plays on the ground): Liberty’s offense turns 11.0% of its runs into explosive gains, and Florida International’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Florida International has the ball (big plays through the air): Florida International’s offense turns 8.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Liberty’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Florida International has the ball (big plays on the ground): Florida International’s offense turns 3.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Liberty’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
contradicting: When Liberty has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Liberty’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.9% of its dropbacks, and Florida International’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.7% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Liberty has the ball (third down): Liberty’s offense converts 41.6% of its third downs, and Florida International’s defense allows opponents to convert 28.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Liberty has the ball (the red zone): Liberty’s offense succeeds on 48.1% of its red-zone plays, and Florida International’s defense allows success on 34.4% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
In his last two games (Delaware and Kennesaw State), Henderson averaged 1.6 yards per attempt, against 12.6 in his two games before that.
quarterbacks: Deshawn Purdie has completed 79 of 134 passes (59.0%) for 1,214 yards, 9.1 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and no interceptions in seven games for Liberty, and has been sacked on 13 of 147 dropbacks.
Jaylen Henderson has completed 7 of 15 passes (46.7%) for 112 yards, 7.5 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games for Liberty, and has been sacked on 0 of 15 dropbacks.

JJ Kohl has completed 131 of 231 passes (56.7%) for 1,657 yards, 7.2 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 8 interceptions in seven games for Florida International, and has been sacked on 7 of 238 dropbacks.
